name: damped_dual_explore_concise
diagnosis: Across 13 unedited base runs (2,210 episodes), Gemma 4 E4B solves 26.31/170 tasks (9 always, 42 sometimes [mean 17.31/42], 119 never). Two coupled failures dominate: (1) premature first edits after little reading (mean first_edit_idx = 4.66 in b6..b12; 34.6% of edit_file calls fail; 30.3% of episodes suffer >=1 failed edit where solve rate drops from 21% to 4%; paired within-task analysis on the 42 unreliable tasks shows failed edits are the strongest failure predictor, 0.30 solved vs 0.60 unsolved, t = -2.53), and (2) verbose thinking that produces bloated fragile old_string quotes (mean 350.5 chars). Across b0..b20, low-dose anti-edit steering (bneg_t0.125: +4.50/batch over 4 runs, 40W/22L, lifting sometimes-tasks to 20.75 and ok_edited to 96.5%) and stacked anti-edit + concise-thinking (bn50_th50: +4.00/batch over 2 runs, cutting old_string to 239.1 chars) were the only repeatable multi-batch winners, whereas colscale (cg_*, b19-b20) lost -3 to -8 tasks/batch. However, bn50_th50 lost 4.2% edit completion (ok_edited = 90.3%) due to (a) overdosing bneg at t=0.5 and (b) a mathematical pathology in neuron.py: near-zero outliers in post_feedforward_layernorm.weight (w_min = 0.0028 at L24, 0.0015 at L26) caused exact coordinate inversion uh = unit(dh / w_post) to collapse write efficiency to 0.266 at L24 and 0.045 at L26, saturating beta = 0.60 and shrinking natural MLP writes by 14.25% (natural_write_scale = 0.8575) on every token.
mechanism: Closed-form rank-1-per-module PEFT LoRA (stored in slot 0 of the standard r=16, lora_alpha=32 template; 18 changed tensors across 6 disjoint layers) overwriting the single quietest MLP neuron j = argmin mean(|a_j|)*||down[:,j]|| per layer using acts_based/acts_base_rl.pt (train split only): (1) Layers 18, 20, 22 (neurons 4218, 2972, 1052): ridge constant gate/up (q.xin ~= 1, gain=4.0) writing -edit@0 (heldout AUC 0.773, 0.813, 0.833) at 0.14 class-gaps/layer (realized bf16 heldout sum = +0.449 gaps, matching the bneg_t0.125 sweet spot). (2) Disjoint layers 24, 26, 28 (neurons 2286, 3105, 9421): ridge constant gate/up writing -th@0 (concise thinking, heldout AUC 0.763, 0.764, 0.755) at 0.12 class-gaps/layer (realized bf16 heldout sum = +0.380 gaps). Crucially, exact division dh / w_post is replaced by Tikhonov-damped preconditioning uh = unit(dh * w_post / (w_post^2 + 0.10 * median(w_post^2))), increasing L26 write efficiency 36x (0.045 -> 1.615) while preserving cos(w_post * uh, dh) in [0.9929, 0.9994], keeping beta in [0.0167, 0.0278] and natural_write_scale in [0.99961, 0.99986] (<=0.04% natural MLP shrinkage at every layer).
predicted_behaviour: Tool calls before first edit (first_edit_idx) rise from 4.7 to 5.7; mean edit_file old_string quote length drops from 351 chars to 285 chars; edit_file call failure rate drops from 34.6% to 30.5% (immediate read_file after failed edit rises from 37.8% to 45.5%); episodes landing >=1 successful edit (ok_edited) stay high at 95.8% (vs 94.5% base and 90.3% in bn50_th50); mean completion tokens remain controlled (~5,950 vs 6,059 base).
predicted_solved_delta: +3.8 solved tasks out of 170 relative to same-batch unedited base (80% interval: [-1.5, +9.0])

name: damped_dual_explore_concise_ctrl
diagnosis: Matched null-direction control for rank-1 edit damped_dual_explore_concise, testing whether any solve-rate change comes from targeting the -edit@0 and -th@0 residual directions versus generic weight-perturbation / greedy-trajectory divergence or natural MLP norm rescaling (across 14 prior norm-matched control runs in b4..b13, mean delta vs same-batch base was -0.07 tasks with single-batch SD 3.38).
mechanism: Identical construction, rank (r=16, lora_alpha=32, slot 0 active), modified layers (18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28), overwritten silent MLP neuron indices (4218, 2972, 1052, 2286, 3105, 9421), ridge constant gate_proj/up_proj rows, Tikhonov damping parameter (0.10), beta values ([0.0167, 0.0278]), and down_proj column norms as damped_dual_explore_concise, except at each layer the target residual direction dh is multiplied by seed-fixed Rademacher signs, orthogonalized to dh, Tikhonov-preconditioned, and projected orthogonal to w_post * dh so cos(w_post * uh_ctrl, dh) = 0.000000 exactly (realized bf16 heldout shift sum = +0.0006 gaps on edit@0 and -0.0010 gaps on th@0, while realized perturbation norms match within <1%).
predicted_behaviour: Agent behaviour remains within run-to-run noise of unedited base: tool calls before first edit ~4.7 (vs 4.7 base), mean edit_file old_string length ~350 chars (vs 351 base), edit_file failure rate ~34.6%, ok_edited ~94.5%, mean completion tokens ~6,060.
predicted_solved_delta: -0.2 solved tasks out of 170 relative to same-batch unedited base (80% interval: [-5.0, +4.5])

name: oproj_onesided_commit_damper
diagnosis: By inverting pre_feedforward_layernorm on xin_i and intersecting with the exact post_attention_layernorm sphere ||(s*v - h_{i-1}) / w_post_attn||^2 = 2560, we reconstructed exact attention writes aw_i and normalized self_attn.o_proj outputs o_norm_i = o_i / rms(o_i) across all 41 layers on acts_based/acts_base_rl.pt (rms accuracy 1.0000-1.0014). This revealed that edit@0 and th@0 enter the residual stream primarily through self_attn.o_proj—especially at global 131k-context full_attention KV-anchor layer 23 (|aw_23|/|h_22| = 4.50x; single-block heldout aw_auc = 0.8191 with gap 43.37 on edit@0, and aw_auc = 0.763 with gap 33.33 on th@0) and layers 17 (FULL), 18, 20, 21—whereas MLPs at those layers slightly reduce heldout AUC. Constant MLP neurons push on every prompt and explore token, while naive symmetric o_proj projection (fold.py) reverses net shift sign at L20/L21 (+0.13 gaps toward editing) because explore writes are non-antipodal.
mechanism: Pure attention edit (self_attn.o_proj only, 8 tensors changed, zero MLP or q_proj changes; slot 0 of r=16, lora_alpha=32). At each edited layer, we compute on the train split the one-sided class-1 o_proj output direction u_i = unit(proj_{orth(span(E[o_norm|label=0], E[o_norm|bg@prompt], E[o_norm|bg@think]))}(E[o_norm|label=1])) via QR orthogonalization and apply rank-1 output attenuation W_o' = (I - gamma_i u_i u_i^T) W_o (B[:,0] = -gamma_i u_i, A[0,:] = 0.5 u_i^T W_o): (1) Premature-edit dampers at L17 (FULL, gamma=0.14), L18, L20, L21 (sliding, gamma=0.16), and L23 (FULL, gamma=0.14): shifts heldout edit@0=1 attention writes by -0.7109 cumulative gaps while shifting edit@0=0 (explore) by only -0.0358 gaps (19.9x one-sided selectivity) and perturbing background attention writes by only 0.7%-2.1%. (2) Verbose-thinking dampers at disjoint layers L24, L26, L28 (gamma=0.14): shifts heldout th@0=1 writes by -0.4196 cumulative gaps vs -0.0414 on concise thinking and 0.6%-0.9% background norm change.
predicted_behaviour: Tool calls before first edit rise from 4.7 to 5.8; mean edit_file old_string length drops from 351 chars to 295 chars; edit_file call failure rate drops from 34.6% to 31.0% (immediate read_file after failed edit rises from 37.8% to 44.5%); ok_edited rises slightly from 94.5% to 95.8% because explore turns and background tokens receive near-zero shift.
predicted_solved_delta: +3.0 solved tasks out of 170 relative to same-batch unedited base (80% interval: [-3.0, +9.0])

name: whitened_cond_rushed_read
diagnosis: Linking acts_based/acts_base_rl.pt to persistent request logs in states_w5d/states.jsonl shows 177 rushed first-edit states (<=4 prior tool calls) vs 300 informed later first-edit states (>=6 prior calls) and 246 explicit read_file calls. Rushed early edits strongly drive the 34.6% edit_file failure rate and the 24.7-task reliability gap on the 42 sometimes-solved tasks, yet constant anti-edit steering at moderate/high dose (bneg_t0.5) keeps pushing against valid late edits and lowers ok_edited from 94.5% to 93.9%. Meanwhile, prior conditional MLP gates (bnegc_t1.0: 22 vs 23) failed because neuron.py --mode cond ignored background states during gate fitting, causing 68.2% background firing leak at L22 (bg_sd = 0.408).
mechanism: Background-whitened conditional MLP neurons at layers 17 (FULL), 18, 20, 22 (neurons 3206, 4218, 2972, 1052; 12 tensors changed in slot 0 of r=16, lora_alpha=32). At each layer, gate_proj[j] is fit in closed form via class-balanced kernel ridge regression on train xin with targets +1.0 on rushed edits (edit@0, label=1, <=4 prior calls), -1.0 on explore (label=0), and -1.5 (2x weight) on bg@prompt + bg@think, affine-anchored with constant ridge readout q (up_proj[j] = q) so max(mean_exp, p98_bg) maps to -1.5 and mean_rush maps to +2.5. On heldout data, rush-vs-explore gate AUC is 0.846-0.878; heldout firing is 0.941-0.996 on rushed edits (<=4 calls), drops 6.7x to 0.103-0.179 on informed edits (>=6 calls), and is 0.0000 on background tokens (|mean| <= 0.00011, sd <= 0.0027). down_proj[:,j] writes the Tikhonov-preconditioned read_file-minus-edit_file residual direction (heldout AUC 0.763-0.872, cos >= 0.9929, natural_write_scale >= 0.9996), delivering +0.7247 cumulative realized heldout gaps toward read_file on rushed commits vs only +0.1083 gaps on informed edits (>=6 calls) and -0.00008 on background.
predicted_behaviour: Rushed early edits (<=4 prior calls) drop substantially, lifting mean tool calls before first edit from 4.7 to 5.5 without inflating late-episode stalls (ok_edited rises from 94.5% to 96.2%); immediate read_file rate after failed edit_file rises from 37.8% to 44.5%, and edit_file call failure rate drops from 34.6% to 31.5%.
predicted_solved_delta: +2.6 solved tasks out of 170 relative to same-batch unedited base (80% interval: [-3.0, +8.5])

name: hybrid_explore_verify_guard
diagnosis: In unedited base runs (b6..b12), 52.0% of edited episodes never run a test command (pytest/unittest/tox) after their final edit, and 85.1% of submitted patches are submitted without a passing test run after the last edit (across b3..b10, 32.4% submit immediately after a failing test, solving only 12% vs 24% when tests pass). Linking acts_bases/acts_base.pt to states_w5s/states.jsonl (369 unverified vs 51 test-verified submit_patch states and 420 run_command states) shows the residual stream linearly encodes unverified submit_patch vs verified submit / run_command with heldout AUC 0.889 at L23 (FULL) and 0.878 at L24. Earlier verification edits (bvfyD_t0.25: 24 vs 26; vfyD_t1.0: 17 vs 24) failed because they injected a constant -sv@0 MLP write at L18,20,22 that fired on all pre-edit tokens, background tokens, and already-verified submit_patch calls.
mechanism: Two-stage closed-form MLP edit across 6 disjoint layers (18 changed tensors in slot 0 of r=16, lora_alpha=32): (1) Pre-edit stage at layers 18, 20, 22 (neurons 4218, 2972, 1052): Tikhonov-damped constant ridge neurons writing -edit@0 at 0.13 gaps/layer (realized bf16 heldout sum = +0.4163 gaps, natural_write_scale >= 0.9998). (2) Post-edit unverified-submit guard at layers 23 (FULL), 24, 28 (neurons 7394, 8788, 9421): cross-dataset whitened conditional ridge gate fit jointly on train splits of acts_bases and acts_based with positive target on unverified submit_patch (sv@0, label=1, t_pass=False) and explicit negative targets on verified submit_patch (t_pass=True), run_command, ok@0, pre-edit edit@0, and background tokens, writing the Tikhonov-preconditioned run_command-minus-unverified-submit direction (heldout write AUC 0.814, 0.853, 0.898; heldout gate AUC 0.829-0.836). Realized bf16 heldout shift toward run_command sums to +0.5690 gaps on unverified submit_patch vs +0.2091 on test-verified submit_patch, +0.0402 on run_command, -0.00006 on pre-edit states, and -0.00005 on background.
predicted_behaviour: Tool calls before first edit rise from 4.7 to 5.3; share of edited episodes running a test command after their last edit (test_after_last_edit) rises from 48.0% to 56.0%, lowering unverified submit_patch rate from 85.1% to 78.5% while preserving overall submit_patch completion (>=94%) and reducing edit_file failure rate from 34.6% to 31.8%.
predicted_solved_delta: +2.3 solved tasks out of 170 relative to same-batch unedited base (80% interval: [-3.5, +8.0])
